propose
ExpEvolve, which injects idea-level extraction and control into evolution: it discovers and leverages
the high-level factors from programs that explain scoring differences among different programs. We
characterize theoretical conditions on when discovery with idea factors improves sample efficiency. We
also build a practical framework to show that the extracted high-level idea factors are helpful for guiding
exploitation from experience and exploration when discovery comes to a plateau. Across11open-ended
mathematical tasks, ExpEvolve significantly improves the final performance and sample efficiency
up to5.0×. The improvements also transfer to4other LLMs and to6machine learning tasks from
MLS-Bench. Analysis shows thatExpEvolve can discover idea-level factors to provide better exploration
and exploitation for evolutionary discovery.

ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
Discovering idea factors from unexplained pairs.The idea discovery process inExpEvolve
is an iterative loop: each time the discovery is triggered,ExpEvolve fits a pairwise ranker on the
annotated idea factors, and selects the pairs of archived programs with a large score gap that the
current idea factors fail to explain. The unexplained pairs suggest theexistence of missing idea factors
that separate the programs in each pair. For the selected pairs, a separate proposer LLM reads the
programs to propose candidate idea factors that distinguish them. Each candidate is then annotated
on the whole archive, and is admitted into the idea memory if each of its values is supported by
enough programs and its values separate the scores.

Exploration at plateaus.Oftentimes, evolutionary discovery can concentrate around its best
programs and a single strategy. Consequently, the ideas widely used in top-scoring programs stop
varying, and their roles cannot be identified from the archive (Thm. 3.3). When the best score does
not improve for𝜅 generations, ExpEvolve switches to idea-guided exploration, which enforces the
mutator LLM to explore diverse ideas other than those widely used in top-scoring programs. Specifi-
cally, a separate LLM probes the properties shared by the top-scoring programs as background idea
factors, and an LLM judge determines which idea factors in the memory depend on the background.
ExpEvolve then masks the actions of the dependent idea factors, instructs the mutator LLM to avoid
them, and assigns more slots to random exploration with diversified demonstrations.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External, objective mathematical verifiers and standard benchmark execution scores (e.g., MLS-Bench objective functions and mathematical constructions).

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains, sample efficiency improvements (up to several-fold fewer evaluations to match baseline scores), and the predictive accuracy of discovered factors over program orderings align well with the empirical data presented in the tables and figures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation benchmarks ExpEvolve against SCS and ShinkaEvolve across 11 established mathematical discovery tasks and integrates it into OpenRSI for 6 MLS-Bench tasks under matched evaluation budgets. Results report seed means, standard deviations, best seeds, and sample efficiency comparisons across multiple underlying LLMs.

evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Internal LLM-driven idea proposing, annotation, ranking, and bandit action selection based on relative performance in previous generation archives.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the studied discovery domains remain restricted to relatively small-scale verification settings with automated/deterministic objective code, leaving expensive real-world verification regimes to future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formalizing evolutionary discovery as a POMDP and grounding the sample complexity gains of structured representations and exploration requirements in Theorems 3.1 and 3.3. Algorithmic steps, LLM prompt templates, pairwise ranker criteria, and plateau heuristics are clearly specified.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides a coherent conceptual framework, rigorous theoretical justification, complete implementation specifics, and solid empirical validation on standard benchmarks without circular evaluation traps.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript introduces ExpEvolve, an evolutionary coding agent framework that extracts interpretable idea-level factors from evaluated programs and uses multi-armed bandits alongside plateau-triggered diversification to guide LLM code mutations, demonstrating improved sample efficiency and task performance across 11 mathematical problems and 6 ML engineering benchmarks.

OpenSaCseparates the agent's research decisions from program
execution. The coding agent chooses the next steps and writes a
Python program that combines software development kit (SDK)
calls with local computation and file operations. The library supplies
typed interfaces for search, content fetching, reranking, and model
calls; the host executes the program. Selected execution results
return to the agent, which decides whether to answer or investigate
further. These observations can include source excerpts, extracted
records, computed summaries, or errors.
Figure 2 illustrates a possible labor-statistics program. Indepen-
dent searches cover unemployment, employment, and earnings
series; the program merges rankings, selects URLs, fetches data,
and retains responses before returning records. Grouping known
requests leaves the agent to identify gaps and decide on follow-up
queries.

Research workflows may require different search services, content
readers, or model endpoints. Provider dispatch separates these back-
end choices from program composition, allowing each capability
to be configured independently.
Adapters map shared capability contracts to each backend's
request and response formats. They register through Python entry
points; the runtime routes calls to the configured adapter for each
capability. Included adapters support Serper and Jina Reader, HTTP
backends, and model endpoints compatible with the OpenAI API.
Users can combine services, replace backends while retaining
program logic, or compare provider configurations with the same
program. Developers can connect new services through custom
adapters without modifying the core library (Figure 2).

evidence.excerpt:
OpenSaCpairs the library with a companion Search as Code skill
that guides agents in composing research programs. The library
supplies executable capabilities; the skill explains when to batch in-
dependent requests, preserve sources, select observations, and reuse
evidence. This guidance is provided through the skill mechanisms
of coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code [2, 6].
The skill works with the agent's existing Python execution and
file tools. Users can revise its guidance to explore different batch-
ing, evidence-selection, and reuse strategies within the same host
workflow.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcomes are measured on established external benchmarks (BrowseComp accuracy, WideSearch macro row F1) with audited decontamination and manual grading corrections, independent of the library and skill design.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: BrowseComp accuracy and WideSearch macro row F1, plus execution time, token counts, and recorded model cost, computed via the Harbor framework on paired task sets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system under study is a fixed open-source library and companion skill with pre-specified guidance; no training, tuning, reward, or selection loop against the reported benchmarks is described.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings align accurately with the evaluation: OpenSaC demonstrated substantial latency and token reductions on both benchmarks, improved BrowseComp accuracy (+2.96%), and showed a minor drop in WideSearch row F1 (-0.84%).

concerns: The study is a single-prompt, single-system, single-domain pilot (n=10 runs of one commercial DRA), and the authors explicitly disclaim generalization, so the empirical contribution is preliminary rather than a robustly validated finding.

The entity extraction and canonicalization pipeline relies on un-audited LLM-based stages (Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini), with no annotation-quality audit or inter-rater validation, leaving the headline Jaccard values subject to unquantified measurement noise.

The evaluation cannot separate retrieval-side from generation-side stochasticity, and exact URL matching conflates web drift and URL-form variability with agent instability, weakening the interpretation of the citation and edge-overlap results.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the representation and questions are intriguing, testing 10 runs of a single prompt on a single black-box agent constitutes preliminary or pilot-level evidence rather than a robust, generalizable benchmark study. The dependence on unvalidated LLM extraction and deduplication without human annotation audits further introduces scientific uncertainty.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The study is a single-prompt, single-system, single-domain pilot (n=10 runs of one commercial DRA), and the authors explicitly disclaim generalization, so the empirical contribution is preliminary rather than a robustly validated finding.

The entity extraction and canonicalization pipeline relies on un-audited LLM-based stages (Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini), with no annotation-quality audit or inter-rater validation, leaving the headline Jaccard values subject to unquantified measurement noise.

The evaluation cannot separate retrieval-side from generation-side stochasticity, and exact URL matching conflates web drift and URL-form variability with agent instability, weakening the interpretation of the citation and edge-overlap results.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves computed over entities extracted and deduplicated by Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini, plus resolved citation URLs.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings accurately reflect the observed run metrics, such as a median pairwise entity Jaccard of 0.12 and citation Jaccard of ~0.01 [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0015, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0016]. However, the claims are inherently constrained by the single-prompt, single-model setup and exact URL matching proxy [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is restricted to n=10 runs of a single prompt on a single commercial system in one domain [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022]. As an empirical characterization, it offers exploratory observations about entity vs citation stability, but the extremely narrow scope limits broader scientific conclusions.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves calculated over entities extracted and deduplicated by Gemini 2.5-flash and gpt-5.4-mini, alongside resolved citation URLs [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0012, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0013].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the commercial deep research agent was queried as a black-box service without parameter tuning or adaptation in this study [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011].

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge major limitations, including reliance on a single prompt, domain, and commercial system, inability to separate retrieval from generation stochasticity, potential web drift, exact URL matching constraints, and un-audited extraction/canonicalization noise [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0022, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology queries Google deep-research-preview 10 times, followed by deterministic preprocessing, entity extraction via Gemini 2.5-flash with langextract, and three-run majority voting canonicalization via gpt-5.4-mini with openai-gabriel [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0012]. The analytical formulation using Jaccard overlap and cumulative discovery curves is clearly defined [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0013, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0014], though the extraction and deduplication stages lack formal validation or human quality auditing [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0024].
primary.quality_rationale: While the representation and questions are intriguing, testing 10 runs of a single prompt on a single black-box agent constitutes preliminary or pilot-level evidence rather than a robust, generalizable benchmark study. The dependence on unvalidated LLM extraction and deduplication without human annotation audits further introduces scientific uncertainty.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript studies the self-consistency of outputs from a commercial deep research agent across 10 repeated queries of a single cybersecurity prompt, analyzing overlap among extracted canonical entities, citation URLs, and entity-citation pairs via pairwise Jaccard similarity and discovery curves [Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0004, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0010, Ea9a6f0d489b70193-B0011].
